title: Imagine being Joshua that morning.
paragraphs: Imagine being Joshua that morning.

You are standing in front of one of the most fortified cities in the region.
Massive stone walls. Armed defenders. No obvious weakness.
And God’s strategy?
Walk.

Not attack.
Not build weapons.
Not storm the gates.
Just walk around the city.
Once a day.
For six days.

No shouting.
No battle cry.
Just obedience.
To any military leader, this plan would sound absurd.
But Joshua understood something powerful:

Victory does not always begin with strength.
Sometimes it begins with surrender.
Joshua’s courage was not proven in a moment of combat.
It was proven in quiet obedience when nothing made sense yet.
Every step around Jericho was an act of faith.
Step after step, they walked around walls that looked impossible to break.
Day after day, nothing changed.

The walls didn’t crack.
The gates didn’t open.
The enemy didn’t surrender.
But Joshua kept walking.
Because faith does not measure progress by what the eyes can see.
It measures progress by what God has said.
Many people abandon obedience because the walls still look the same after the first lap.
Or the second.
Or the third.
But Jericho reminds us of something profound:
God is often working during the silent laps.
The miracle didn’t start on the seventh day.
It started the moment Joshua chose to obey a strategy that required courage, humility, and trust.
Sometimes the most powerful faith is not loud.
It’s the faith that keeps walking.
Even when the walls are still standing.
Memorable Lines from This Lesson

• “Faith sometimes looks like walking around a problem that only God can bring down.”
• “The walls didn’t fall because of noise. They fell because of obedience.”
• “God often works during the silent laps.”
• “Joshua’s courage was not in the battle—it was in the trust.”
So here’s the question:
What wall in your life might God be asking you to keep walking around in faith?
